overall: Atlanta is experiencing a warm but moderating mid-June afternoon, with the running maximum stalling at 80.6°F for the past 50 minutes despite it being nearly 4 PM ET — prime heating hours. The day warmed steadily through midday but has lost all upward momentum, with a velocity of +0.0°F/hr suggesting the peak may already be in or very nearly so. The dewpoint of 60.8°F and 9.2 mph winds are modest but sufficient to limit further boundary-layer heating.
forecast_obs_notes: Models (ECMWF 82.8°F, HRRR 82.9°F, NBM 82.3°F) are running 1.7–2.3°F above the current observed running max, a meaningful warm bias that has not been borne out by observations. The ensemble signals are divergent and both above current observed temps — the even model's 84–85°F Tier 4 (Avoid) signal appears especially unreliable given real-time data, while the odd model's 83–84°F Tier 2 signal still requires a nearly 3°F surge in the final hours, which the flat velocity does not support.
max_temp_prediction: With zero upward velocity at 15:50 ET and Atlanta's June peak heating window essentially closing, the probability of a meaningful additional rise to reach model targets is low. A small residual uptick of 0.3–0.5°F is possible if a brief mixing event occurs, but the stall is a strong signal that 80.6°F is at or very near the daily high. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the final TMAX will land in the 80.5–81.5°F range, well below all three deterministic model forecasts.
